items.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024
items.q: Pullen and John Hicks and Billy Hart — all these great musicians that I admire

ctx.x: Sure is. Really is. Especially right now. You know because the — how do we say it — not the template, but what has worked for so long does not work as well anymore. So what we’ve been conditioned in the last — rehearse a band, go out on tour, come home, make a record, everybody you know goes and does their own thing for a bit, then come back together. Yeah, it’s — with the clubs, you know so many of the clubs, arts presenters, funding cut back for the art presenters received. It’s in a changing environment for…

Pullen and John Hicks and Billy Hart — all these great musicians that I admire, they’ve all just lived off their musical performance. Their playing. Their artistic endeavors. Their creative drive and their expertise in being hired. That’s gone. So I don’t know. It’s just different to really have to, in my case I’m trying to maybe open up a bit more to collaborating with more musicians and so that will allow me to stay in a creative space which is what I really thrive on. I love collaborating, I love throwing…

Have you ever had a student at one of these perhaps workshops ask you if you use a particular jazz technique and you don’t really know what they’re talking about? I mean it’s happened to me. Something that they’ve learned from a book or some video on YouTube. So when do you use that?
